union.text: Sichuan as the Ming province stood: Sichuan with the Chongqing area

land.text: the Ming lands Zhang Xianzhong took: Wuchang and Macheng (1643), 'much of Hunan', then Chongqing (25 July 1644), Chengdu (9 September 1644) and 'most of Sichuan province'

predecessors.note: The infobox reads 'Preceded by: Ming dynasty'. The Ming dossier ends in April 1644, before Chongqing and Chengdu fell, so the Sichuan gains are recorded here from the Xi side.

land.text: Sichuan: 'its territory fell to the forces of the Southern Ming and the Manchu-led Qing dynasty' (infobox); the page gives no boundary between them

successors.note: Most of Sichuan was not under Qing control 'until a dozen years or so later' (Zhang Xianzhong page); fighting 'finally ended in eastern Sichuan in 1664'.

land.text: Sichuan: the same sentence names the Southern Ming; the generals' remnants 'held out in Sichuan, Yunnan, and Guizhou'

successors.note: The remnant armies of Li Dingguo and Sun Kewang, not a state: in 1647 they 'took Chongqing in Sichuan and took Guiyang in Guizhou' (Li Dingguo page) and first aided Ming loyalists in 1648. No dossier covers the remnant as its own state.

capitals.name: Huangzhou
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Huangzhou (1643)'. The Zhang Xianzhong page has him set up a government at Wuchang and abandon it 'after two months'; the two pages are not reconciled.

capitals.name: Chengdu (Xijing)
capitals.note: 'He took Chengdu on 9 September 1644' and 'set up court in Chengdu, which he renamed Xijing (Western Capital)'; infobox 'Chengdu (1644-1647)'.

rulers.name: Zhang Xianzhong
rulers.title: Xi Wang (King of the West) 1643; emperor of the Xi, era name Dashun, from 1644
rulers.note: Infobox: proclaimed king 1643, emperor 1644, reign 1643-1647. The Zhang page puts the emperor's proclamation in the 10th lunar month of 1644; he died on 2 January 1647 (infobox) at Xichong.

correction.text: Wuchang, Macheng and Hunan: the places Zhang Xianzhong's page names in 1643; the unnamed 'part of Jiangxi' is not drawn

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a rebel state Cliopatria lacks. Zhang 'captured the provincial capital of Wuchang, killed the imperial prince there, and proclaimed himself Xi Wang'; 'he took Macheng in Huguang'; at Changsha he 'controlled much of Hunan and part of Jiangxi'. The page dates the proclamation to 1643 but gives no date for the Hunan control; the part of Jiangxi is not named, so it is not drawn.

correction.text: Sichuan as the Ming province stood: Sichuan with the Chongqing area

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the Xi in Sichuan. 'Chongqing ... 25 July 1644' and 'He took Chengdu on 9 September 1644' (Zhang page); the Xi page: 'based at Chengdu since 1644' and 'ruled most of Sichuan province'. No boundary is given; the drawn shape is Sichuan with the Chongqing area, as a province of the Ming.

minus.text: Sichuan as the Ming province stood: Sichuan with the Chongqing area

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Chongqing was retaken by Ming loyalists in the spring of 1645'; the rest of Sichuan stays Zhang's until 'In October 1646, Zhang abandoned Sichuan. He headed towards his homeland in Shaanxi.' By then his government 'had virtually disintegrated'; the shape holds to the abandonment.

ledger.note: 1643: Zhang Xianzhong takes Wuchang and proclaims himself Xi Wang. Zhang page: he 'captured the provincial capital of Wuchang, killed the imperial prince there, and proclaimed himself "Xi Wang" (King of the West)'; 'he took Macheng in Huguang'. Infobox 'Proclamation as King: 1643'. The pages give no month.

region.text: Hunan ('much of'); the part of Jiangxi is not named

ledger.note: 1643: Zhang controls much of Hunan. At Changsha he 'controlled much of Hunan and part of Jiangxi'. The page dates the proclamation to 1643 and the move into Sichuan to 1644 but gives no year for Hunan, so the year is the sequence's; the unnamed part of Jiangxi is not drawn.

1643: Zhang abandons Wuchang. He 'attempted to set up a government in Wuchang, but abandoned the city after two months'; Ming forces 'then retook it soon after Zhang left'. No month is given, so the year follows from the 1643 capture.

1644: Zhang takes the imperial title. 'In the 10th lunar month of 1644 he declared himself as emperor with the reign title Dashun' and declared the 'Xi dynasty (Great Western dynasty)'. The page gives no Gregorian date, so the event has no month and sorts first in the year. Same state, same colour.
1644: Zhang takes Chongqing. 'Captured the city on 25 July 1644.' The counterpart is the Ming: the Ming dossier ended in April 1644, and the page names no other holder.

region.text: Sichuan as the Ming province stood: Sichuan with the Chongqing area

ledger.note: 1644: Zhang takes Chengdu and the Xi rule most of Sichuan. 'He took Chengdu on 9 September 1644' and renamed it Xijing; the Xi page: 'based at Chengdu since 1644', 'ruled most of Sichuan province'. The city and year are the pages'; the province is the page's phrase with no boundary.
1644: the court moves to Chengdu. 'Set up court in Chengdu, which he renamed Xijing'; infobox 'Capital: Huangzhou (1643); Chengdu (1644-1647)'.

1645: Ming loyalists retake Chongqing. 'Chongqing was retaken by Ming loyalists in the spring of 1645.' The counterpart is the Southern Ming (the Hongguang court, June 1644 to June 1645), my reading of 'Ming loyalists'.

minus.text: Sichuan as the Ming province stood: Sichuan with the Chongqing area

ledger.note: 1646: Zhang abandons Sichuan. 'In October 1646, Zhang abandoned Sichuan. He headed towards his homeland in Shaanxi.' His government 'had virtually disintegrated'. The page names no taker; the infobox later gives the territory to the Southern Ming and the Qing, undated.

region.text: Xichong, where Zhang died (nearest gazetteer place Nanchong)

ledger.note: 1647: the dynasty ends. 'The dynasty ended in 1647 after the death of Zhang Xianzhong'; infobox date 2 January 1647, at Xichong, where the Qing forces met him. His generals Li Dingguo, Sun Kewang, Liu Wenxiu and Ai Nengqi led the remnants, which 'held out in Sichuan, Yunnan, and Guizhou'.

wars.name: Zhang Xianzhong's conquest of Sichuan

zones.text: Sichuan as the Ming province stood: Sichuan with the Chongqing area

wars.outcome: Chongqing fell on 25 July 1644 and Chengdu on 9 September 1644; Ming loyalists retook Chongqing in spring 1645.

wars.name: Qing campaign against Zhang Xianzhong

zones.text: Xichong, where Zhang had set up camp (nearest gazetteer place Nanchong)

wars.outcome: Zhang left Sichuan in October 1646 and was killed at Xichong on 2 January 1647 (infobox); the Xi ended.
wars.note: The page says 'Zhang and the Qing forces met in Xichong'.

certainty.note: A mobile rebel regime: the pages name cities (Wuchang, Chongqing, Chengdu) and provinces ('much of Hunan', 'most of Sichuan') but no boundary.

sources.title: Zhang Xianzhong
sources.note: Wuchang and Xi Wang 1643, Changsha ('much of Hunan'), Chongqing 25 July and Chengdu 9 September 1644, the Dashun emperor in the 10th lunar month, Chongqing retaken spring 1645, Sichuan abandoned October 1646, death at Xichong January 1647.

sources.note: Infobox (names, capitals Huangzhou 1643 and Chengdu 1644-1647, king 1643, emperor 1644, abolished 1647, succeeded by Qing and Southern Ming); 'ruled most of Sichuan province'; no area or boundary.

notes:
Written by ea-07 on 2026-10-25 from three pages (budget 2-5). Zhang Xianzhong's Xi is a rebel state Cliopatria lacks: its Li Zicheng row covers the Shun only, so the three keyframes are new (xi-dynasty_1643, _1644, _1645) and no Cliopatria shape is reviewed. In the Cliopatria Ming shapes of 1632-1644 the Sichuan cells are Ming land; the ming-dynasty dossier records the 1643 Wuchang and Hunan loss to the Xi, and this dossier records the 1644 Sichuan gains from the Xi side only.

Not settled: where the Xi held ground in 1643 (the Xi infobox names Huangzhou, the Zhang page Wuchang and Changsha, and the page's 'part of Jiangxi' names no city, so it is not drawn); the year of the Hunan control (the page gives none); whether Zhang held all of Sichuan in 1645-46 (the Xi page says 'most', and the 1645-46 shape is Sichuan less the Chongqing area, soft); who took the land when he left in October 1646 (counterpart 'nobody'; the infobox gives it to the Southern Ming and the Qing without years); and the Xi remnants of 1647-59 under Li Dingguo and Sun Kewang, which hold Guizhou, Chongqing and Yunnan as allies of the Southern Ming (Li Dingguo page) and have no dossier: the Sun Kewang page does not exist under that title on Wikipedia (failed at its site), so the Li Dingguo page was used. The Chongqing admin-1 unit is wider than the city (it covers eastern Sichuan of the Ming), which suits the Ming province but may overdraw the Xi's hold in 1644-45.

Counterparts: 'ming-dynasty' for the 1643-44 gains (the Ming dossier ends in April 1644, before Chongqing and Chengdu fell), 'southern-ming' for Chongqing in 1645 (my reading of 'Ming loyalists'), 'nobody' for the October 1646 abandonment, 'qing-dynasty' on the dissolve.
